_note: Copy to maps/<map>.json and fill in. Every '_note' key is documentation and is ignored by the tools; delete them or keep them, as you like. maps/pgg.json is a complete filled-in example. Run 'python check_config.py <map>' before stage 1: it reports missing and inconsistent keys.
title: Game title, edition, which printing this image is

sources._note: 'primary' is the image whose pixel frame the sheet follows. Add other editions as further named sources; each needs its own control_points and fit. size_hint is the approximate circumradius in pixels (centre to a corner), read off a ruler crop in stage 0. line_dark is the grey level under which a pixel counts as grid-line ink.

primary.note: pixel size, and any other file that is the same image

control_points._note: stage 1 fills this in: at least 12 hexes, one in each of the nine regions (four corners, four edge middles, centre)

grid._note: orientation 'flat' or 'pointy'; offset 'odd' or 'even' (which printed columns, or rows on a pointy grid, are shifted down); id-format is a Python format over col and row; id-side is the hexside the PRINTED id sits against, so the overlay puts our id opposite it; terrain is the default terrain of a hex nothing else claims; extent names printed ids that must be on the grid.

tiles._note: a reader's tile: core hexes square, margin hexes all round, scale of the crop

vocabulary._note: How THIS print draws each feature, in words a reader can match by eye, colours included. The ids must be the sheet's own terrain, glyph and line ids. Pasted into the reader prompt.

terrain.clear: how the print draws it, with colours
terrain.woods: how the print draws it, with colours
terrain.swamp: how the print draws it, with colours
terrain.lake: how the print draws it, with colours

hexside_lines.river: how the print draws it, and what it is NOT (a lake outline of the same colour)

markers.entrance: margin furniture a person reads in the edge pass

candidates._note: Stage 4. colour_masks: per feature either 'rgb' (a list of colours) with 'tol', or a 'green' hue rule {over_r, over_b, min_r}; optional 'open' (drop thin strokes, in px), 'close' (fill mottle), 'grow' (bridge gaps). hex_masks are the masks measured per hex. THRESHOLDS ARE NOT GUESSES: set every 'at_least' from the person's labelled hexes (stage 0 step 5), in a gap of the measured distribution just under the faintest hex they call that terrain. Order matters: a hatch or symbol terrain (swamp) must come before a blob-colour terrain (woods) whose mask its strokes partly match. blob_share and blob_cover catch a symbol drawn wholly inside one hex.

presence._note: a link's own coverage a hex needs before a crossing counts as a step

sheet._note: path and png are relative to map_graphics/xml. urban is REQUIRED by hexsheet.xsd: 'buildings' (a pale tint with scattered black rectangles) or 'symbol' (a plain glyph), how the renderer draws cities. keep lists the parts of an existing sheet copied through unchanged.
